column1: Your game library. Every game is a **profile**: GameTimeNext records how long you play it, keeps track of your playthroughs and shows your progress. Running games are detected automatically, so GameTimeNext will switch to the correct profile.

3. Save, then start the game as usual.
> For Steam games use **Steam import** in the profile: name, game folder and data are filled in for you.
> You can also start steam linked games via GameTimeNext (""Launch"" button)

- **Cancel current playthrough**: ends it without completing it
- **Start new playthrough**: begins a new run

All settings of GameTimeNext in one place: how playtime is recorded, hotkeys, backups, the look of the app and the connections to SteamGridDB and IGDB. The pages are on the left: **General**, **Monitoring**, **Tags** and **About**.
> Changes are saved as you make them. Click **Save settings** to apply the accent colors and the background right away.

column3: What it does
**Ctrl + B** turns all monitors black, e.g. to protect OLED displays during a break. Press it again to end the blackout.
Shows an animated particle clock on the black screens. Only available with the blackout key combination.
Starts GameTimeNext with Windows, minimized in the background.
While playtime is being recorded, a notification reminds you to take a break every *n* hours of the current session. Enter the hours in the field next to it.

column1: - **API key**: needed to search game covers on SteamGridDB (in a profile: **SteamGridDB…**).
- The ↗ button opens SteamGridDB, where you can sign in and create your free API key.
IGDB provides the **estimated playtimes** (*Story*, *Story + Extras*, *Completionist*) of your games.
- **Enable Integration**: when you save a profile, its estimated playtimes are loaded from IGDB.
- **Client ID** / **Client Secret**: your Twitch developer credentials. The ↗ buttons open the IGDB guide that explains how to get them.
> The **progress bar** in the profile details is only shown when Client ID and Client Secret are entered.
- **Allow profile-specific colors**: the app may take on the accent colors of the active profile. The profile itself must have *Change accent colors based on this profile* switched on as well.
- **Dynamic Background**: blurred image behind the main window
- *Profile dependent*: the cover of the selected profile

All games you played in the period, the most recently played first. Each entry shows the cover, the name, when you last played the game and its playtime in the period.
> - Sessions that cross the start or end of the period only count with the part that lies inside it. A session from 23:00 to 01:00 counts one hour for each of the two days.
> - Such a session also counts as a played day for **both** days in **Days Played**.
> - If nothing was played in the period, the cards show **n.A.**

A **playthrough** is one run through a game: your first run, a second run, a DLC or anything else you want to track separately. All playtime is recorded in a playthrough, so you can see how long each run took. This app lists the playthroughs of all your games and lets you manage them.
- Every game has **at most one running playthrough**. Playtime is always recorded in it.
- If no playthrough is running when you start a game, GameTimeNext asks whether a new one should be started.
- A playthrough is in one of these states:

column3: Meaning
The active run, playtime is recorded here.
Put aside for now, can be continued later.
Finished.
Abandoned. Its playtime still counts in your total playtime.
Use
Your first run of a game.
Every further run, e.g. a second run on a higher difficulty.
Playtime of a DLC or expansion.
Anything else you want to keep separate.

Codetables are the **selection lists** of GameTimeNext: every value you can pick in a dropdown, e.g. the **platform** of a game, comes from a codetable. Here you can look at all codetables and extend the ones that are meant for you, e.g. add your own platform with its own symbol.

column3: Meaning
One selection list, e.g. *Platform*. It is identified by its short **text type**, e.g. `pF`.
One value of the list, e.g. *Playstation 5*.
The short, unique key of an entry, e.g. `PS5`. GameTimeNext stores this key, the **description** is what you see in the app.
Some codetables store extra information per entry, e.g. a platform has a *Platform-Type* and a *Symbol*.
*User*: you can add and change entries. *Developer*: maintained by GameTimeNext, you can only view them.
